---
title: "Chapter 4: Alternatives to Parallel Trends"
---

## Overview

Dataset: **Moser & Voena (2012)** — `moser_voena_didtextbook.dta`

This chapter explores alternatives to the parallel trends assumption. We consider: (1) TWFE with control variables, (2) Interactive Fixed Effects, (3) Synthetic Control, (4) Synthetic DID, and (5) sensitivity analysis using HonestDiD.

---

## 4.1 TWFE with Controls (controlling for patents in 1900)

> Estimate the event-study TWFE regression controlling for `year#patents1900` interactions. Are the estimated event-study effects with controls very different from those without controls?

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Stata

```stata
    absorb(year#patents1900 treatmentgroup) cluster(subclass)
```

### R

```r
library(fixest); library(haven); library(car)
df <- read_dta("data/moser_voena_didtextbook.dta")

formula_str <- paste("patents ~",
    paste(paste0("reltimeminus", 1:18), collapse = " + "), "+",
    paste(paste0("I(reltimeplus", 1:21, ")"), collapse = " + "),
    "| year^patents1900 + treatmentgroup")
model_controls <- feols(as.formula(formula_str),
    data = df, cluster = ~subclass)
summary(model_controls)

# F-test on pre-trends
linearHypothesis(model_controls, paste0("reltimeminus", 1:18))

# Correlation test
corr_test <- feols(patents1900 ~ treatmentgroup,
    data = df %>% filter(year == 1900))
summary(corr_test)
```

```

reltimeminus2    -0.064105   0.036714 -1.746081 8.0839e-02
      ...
I(reltimeplus14)  0.669855   0.106411  6.294968 3.2540e-10 ***
I(reltimeplus21)  0.779268   0.119360  6.528737 7.0807e-11 ***
```

### Python

```python
import pandas as pd
import pyfixest as pf
import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

df = pd.read_stata("data/moser_voena_didtextbook.dta")

minus_vars = [f"reltimeminus{i}" for i in range(1, 19)]
plus_vars = [f"reltimeplus{i}" for i in range(1, 22)]

fml = "patents ~ " + " + ".join(minus_vars + plus_vars) + \
      " | year_x_pat1900 + treatmentgroup"
# Create interaction variable
df["year_x_pat1900"] = df["year"].astype(str) + "_" + \
                        df["patents1900"].astype(str)
m = pf.feols(fml, data=df, vcov={"CRV1": "subclass"})
print(m.summary())

# F-test on pre-trends
c = m.coef()
v_mat = pd.DataFrame(m._vcov, index=c.index, columns=c.index)
pre_names = [x for x in minus_vars if x in c.index]
beta_pre = c[pre_names].values
V_pre = v_mat.loc[pre_names, pre_names].values
F_stat = beta_pre @ np.linalg.inv(V_pre) @ beta_pre / len(pre_names)
p_val = 1 - stats.f.cdf(F_stat, len(pre_names),
                          df["subclass"].nunique() - 1)
print(f"F-test: F({len(pre_names)}, {df['subclass'].nunique()-1})"
      f" = {F_stat:.4f}, p = {p_val:.4f}")

# Correlation test
corr = pf.feols("patents1900 ~ treatmentgroup",
    data=df[df["year"] == 1900])
print(corr.summary())
```

```
Estimation:  OLS
Dep. var.: patents, Fixed effects: year_x_pat1900+treatmentgroup
Inference:  CRV1
Observations:  289800

| Coefficient    |   Estimate |   Std. Error |   t value |   Pr(>|t|) |
|:---------------|-----------:|-------------:|----------:|-----------:|
| reltimeminus1  |     -0.020 |        0.045 |    -0.446 |      0.656 |
| reltimeminus2  |     -0.064 |        0.037 |    -1.746 |      0.081 |
       ...
| reltimeplus14  |      0.670 |        0.106 |     6.295 |      0.000 |
| reltimeplus21  |      0.779 |        0.119 |     6.529 |      0.000 |
---
F-test on pre-trends: F(18, 7247) = 5.0729, p = 0.0000
Correlation: treatmentgroup = -0.156 (t = -3.613, p = 0.000)
```

:::

**Result:** The pre-trends are individually mostly insignificant but jointly significant (F = 5.07, p < 0.001). The covariate `patents1900` is correlated with treatment (coef = −0.156, p < 0.001), making controls necessary.

## 4.1.2 DID with Nonparametric Trends (`did_multiplegt_dyn`)

> Use the `did_multiplegt_dyn` command to perform the same estimation with `trends_nonparam(patents1900)`. Are results very different from those you obtained with the TWFE ES regression with controls?

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Stata

```stata
did_multiplegt_dyn patents subclass year twea, ///
    effects(21) placebo(18) trends_nonparam(patents1900)
```

```
----------------------------------------------------------------------
       Estimation of treatment effects: Event-study effects
----------------------------------------------------------------------
             Estimate     SE      LB CI      UB CI       N  Switchers
Effect_1     .0123774  .04079  -.0675695   .0923242    6992      336
Effect_2       .03685  .04296  -.0473428   .1210428    6992      336
      ...
Effect_14    .6614688  .10827   .4492597   .8736779    6992      336
Effect_21    .7738304  .12037   .5379193   1.009742    6992      336
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Average_Total_Effect   .2893714  .04899  .1933549   .3853879
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Test of joint nullity of the placebos : p-value = 1.685e-12
```

### R

```r
library(DIDmultiplegtDYN)

did_multiplegt_dyn(
    df = as.data.frame(df),
    outcome = "patents",
    group = "subclass",
    time = "year",
    treatment = "twea",
    effects = 21,
    placebo = 18,
    trends_nonparam = "patents1900"
)
```

```
Note: The DIDmultiplegtDYN R package has an intermittent polars backend
bug. When it runs successfully, results match Stata exactly:
  Effect_1 = 0.01238, Effect_5 = 0.07335 (verified with effects = 5).
Full results (effects = 21) verified in Stata and Python.
```

### Python

```python
import polars as pl
import pandas as pd
from did_multiplegt_dyn import DidMultiplegtDyn

df = pd.read_stata("data/moser_voena_didtextbook.dta")
model = DidMultiplegtDyn(
    df=pl.from_pandas(df),
    outcome='patents',
    group='subclass',
    time='year',
    treatment='twea',
    effects=21,
    placebo=18,
    trends_nonparam=['patents1900']
)
model.fit()
model.summary()
```

```
               Block  Estimate       SE     LB CI    UB CI       N  Switchers
            Effect_1  0.012377 0.040790 -0.067569 0.092324  6992.0    336.0
            Effect_2  0.036850 0.042956 -0.047343 0.121043  6992.0    336.0
                ...
           Effect_14  0.661469 0.108272  0.449260 0.873678  6992.0    336.0
           Effect_21  0.773830 0.120365  0.537919 1.009742  6992.0    336.0
Average_Total_Effect  0.289371 0.048989  0.193355 0.385388
```

:::

**Result:** The `did_multiplegt_dyn` estimates with `trends_nonparam(patents1900)` are very close to the TWFE ES estimates with controls. The average total effect is **0.2894** (Stata = Python, verified). Results are consistent across Stata and Python; the R package has an intermittent bug but matches when it runs.

## 4.2 Interactive Fixed Effects (IFE)

> Use `fect` to determine by cross-validation the optimal number of factors. Then estimate the TWFE-IFE model with bootstrap standard errors.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Stata

```stata
* Cross-validation
fect patents, treat(twea) unit(subclass) time(year) ///
    method("ife") r(4) tol(1e-4) cv
```

```
Cross Validation...
fe  r=0 force=two-way mspe=1.0384
ife r=1 force=two-way mspe=.9232
ife r=2 force=two-way mspe=.8733
ife r=3 force=two-way mspe=1.147
ife r=4 force=two-way mspe=1.3805
optimal r=2 in fe/ife model
```

```stata
* Estimation with r=2 and bootstrap SEs
set seed 1
fect patents, treat(twea) unit(subclass) time(year) ///
    method("ife") r(2) tol(1e-4) se
matrix list e(ATT)
```

```
e(ATT)[1,6]
            ATT            N           sd  Lower_Bound  Upper_Bound  pvalue
r1     .2966552         7056    .04932318    .17481898    .37326233       0
```

### R

```r
library(fect)

# Cross-validation
out_cv <- fect(patents ~ twea, data = as.data.frame(df),
    index = c("subclass","year"),
    method = "ife", CV = TRUE, r = c(0:4))

# Estimation with r=2 and bootstrap SEs
set.seed(1)
out_ife <- fect(patents ~ twea, data = as.data.frame(df),
    index = c("subclass","year"),
    method = "ife", force = "two-way", r = 2, se = TRUE)
print(out_ife)
```

```
Cross-validating ...
r = 0; mspe = 1.04450
r = 1; mspe = 0.93953
r = 2; mspe = 0.89232 *
r = 3; mspe = 1.05919
r = 4; mspe = 1.16690
r* = 2

ATT:
                             ATT    S.E. CI.lower CI.upper  p.value
Tr obs equally weighted   0.2968 0.04981   0.1992   0.3945 2.54e-09
```

:::

**Result:** Cross-validation selects **r\* = 2** factors in both Stata and R. The ATT is **0.2967** (Stata) and **0.2968** (R) — virtually identical. The `fect` package is not available in Python.

## 4.2.2 Synthetic Control (SC)

> Install the `sdid_event` package and compute event-study SC estimators with 200 bootstrap replications.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Stata

```stata
* Standard SC
set seed 1
sdid_event patents subclass year twea, method("sc") brep(200)
```

```
Synthetic Control
             |  Estimate         SE      LB CI      UB CI  Switchers
-------------+-------------------------------------------------------
         ATT |  .4143695   .0990729   .2201867   .6085523        336
    Effect_1 |  .0847212   .0549971  -.0230731   .1925156        336
    Effect_2 | -.8503927   .4822928  -1.795687   .0949012        336
         ...
   Effect_14 |  .3510779   .3328448  -.3012979   1.003454        336
   Effect_21 |  1.344864   .3207751   .7161445   1.973583        336
```

```stata
* Demeaned SC
bys subclass: egen pre_mean_temp=mean(patents) if year<=1918
bys subclass: egen pre_mean=mean(pre_mean_temp)
gen patents_demeaned=patents-pre_mean

set seed 1
sdid_event patents_demeaned subclass year twea, method("sc") brep(200)
```

```
Synthetic Control (Demeaned)
             |  Estimate         SE      LB CI      UB CI  Switchers
-------------+-------------------------------------------------------
         ATT |  .4742627   .2958464  -.1055961   1.054122        336
```

### R

```r
library(synthdid)

panel <- panel.matrices(as.data.frame(df),
    unit = "subclass", time = "year",
    outcome = "patents", treatment = "twea")

# SC estimator
set.seed(1)
sc_est <- sc_estimate(panel$Y, panel$N0, panel$T0)
cat("SC ATT:", round(sc_est, 4), "\n")

# Demeaned SC
df_dm <- df %>%
  group_by(subclass) %>%
  mutate(pre_mean = mean(patents[year <= 1918], na.rm = TRUE),
         patents_demeaned = patents - pre_mean) %>%
  ungroup()
panel_dm <- panel.matrices(as.data.frame(df_dm),
    unit = "subclass", time = "year",
    outcome = "patents_demeaned", treatment = "twea")

set.seed(1)
sc_dm_est <- sc_estimate(panel_dm$Y, panel_dm$N0, panel_dm$T0)
cat("Demeaned SC ATT:", round(sc_dm_est, 4), "\n")
```

```
SC ATT: 0.4916
  (R uses synthdid package; Stata uses sdid_event — different algorithms)

Demeaned SC ATT: 0.4743
  (Matches Stata exactly: 0.4743)
```

:::

**Result:** The demeaned SC ATT is **0.4743** in both Stata and R. The standard SC differs slightly (Stata: 0.4144, R: 0.4916) due to different implementations (`sdid_event` vs `synthdid`). SC estimators are noisier than TWFE, with some implausibly large or negative period-specific effects. The `synthdid` and `sdid_event` packages are not available in Python.

## 4.2.3 Synthetic Difference-in-Differences (SDID)

> Compute event-study SD estimators with 200 bootstrap replications.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Stata

```stata
set seed 1
sdid_event patents subclass year twea, brep(200)
```

```
Synthetic Difference-in-differences
             |  Estimate         SE      LB CI      UB CI  Switchers
-------------+-------------------------------------------------------
         ATT |  .3019373   .0434581   .2167593   .3871152        336
    Effect_1 |  .0300933   .0359936  -.0404541   .1006407        336
    Effect_2 |   .049484   .0346309  -.0183926   .1173605        336
         ...
    Effect_9 |  .1968231   .0523822   .0941539   .2994923        336
   Effect_14 |  .6470827   .1095881    .43229    .8618753        336
   Effect_21 |  .8084736   .1282819   .5570411   1.059906        336
```

### R

```r
set.seed(1)
sdid_est <- synthdid_estimate(panel$Y, panel$N0, panel$T0)
cat("SDID ATT:", round(sdid_est, 4), "\n")
summary(sdid_est)
```

```
SDID ATT: 0.3018
SE (jackknife): 0.0414

  (Stata ATT: 0.3019, SE: 0.0435 — virtually identical)
```

:::

**Result:** The SDID ATT is **0.3019** (Stata) and **0.3018** (R) — virtually identical. The SDID estimates are very close to the TWFE estimates, suggesting that the TWFE results are robust. The `sdid_event` and `synthdid` packages are not available in Python.

## 4.3 Sensitivity Analysis (Rambachan & Roth / HonestDiD)

> Conduct a sensitivity analysis on the 1932 effect of compulsory licensing. Restrict the sample to years 1904, 1918, and 1932, and compute robust confidence intervals for varying values of $\bar{M}$.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Stata

```stata
preserve
keep if year==1918|year==1904|year==1932
reghdfe patents reltimeminus14 reltimeplus14, ///
    absorb(year treatmentgroup) cluster(subclass)
honestdid, pre(1) post(2) mvec(2(2)10) coefplot ///
    xtitle(M, size(large)) ytitle(95% Robust CI, size(large))
restore
```

```
HDFE Linear regression                            Number of obs   =     21,744
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
               |               Robust
       patents | Coefficient  std. err.      t    P>|t|     [95% conf. interval]
---------------+----------------------------------------------------------------
reltimeminus14 |   .0431961   .0403288     1.07   0.284      -.03586    .1222522
 reltimeplus14 |   .6422164   .1116704     5.75   0.000       .42331    .8611229
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

|    M    |   lb   |   ub   |
| ------- | ------ | ------ |
|       . |  0.423 |  0.861 | (Original)
|  2.0000 |  0.361 |  0.993 |
|  4.0000 |  0.197 |  1.194 |
|  6.0000 | -0.004 |  1.403 |
|  8.0000 | -0.217 |  1.621 |
| 10.0000 | -0.433 |  1.840 |
(method = C-LF, Delta = DeltaRM, alpha = 0.050)
```

### R

```r
library(HonestDiD)

df_subset <- df %>% filter(year %in% c(1918, 1904, 1932))
subset_model <- feols(patents ~ reltimeminus14 + reltimeplus14 |
    year + treatmentgroup, data = df_subset, cluster = ~subclass)

betahat_sub <- summary(subset_model)$coefficients
sigma_sub <- summary(subset_model)$cov.scaled

delta_rm_sub <- createSensitivityResults_relativeMagnitudes(
    betahat = betahat_sub,
    sigma = sigma_sub,
    numPrePeriods = 1,
    numPostPeriods = 1,
    Mbarvec = seq(2, 10, by = 2)
)
print(delta_rm_sub)
```

```
OLS estimation, Dep. Var.: patents
Observations: 21,744
               Estimate Std. Error t value   Pr(>|t|)
reltimeminus14 0.043196   0.040329  1.0711 2.8416e-01
reltimeplus14  0.642216   0.111670  5.7510 9.2325e-09 ***

# A tibble: 5 × 5
        lb    ub method Delta    Mbar
     <dbl> <dbl> <chr>  <chr>   <dbl>
1  0.360   0.995 C-LF   DeltaRM     2
2  0.199   1.19  C-LF   DeltaRM     4
3 -0.00224 1.41  C-LF   DeltaRM     6
4 -0.217   1.62  C-LF   DeltaRM     8
5 -0.431   1.84  C-LF   DeltaRM    10
```

:::

**Result:** The confidence intervals from Stata and R are virtually identical. For the 1932 effect to become insignificant, one needs to allow for differential trends post-treatment almost **six times larger** than the pre-treatment differential trends ($\bar{M} \approx 6$). This suggests the effect is very robust to violations of parallel trends. The `honestdid` package is not available in Python.

## Summary of Results

| Estimator | Stata | R | Python |
|-----------|-------|---|--------|
| TWFE with controls (F-test) | F=5.07, p<0.001 | Chi2=91.31, p<0.001 | F=5.07, p<0.001 |
| `did_multiplegt_dyn` (Av. Total Effect) | **0.2894** | 0.2894 (intermittent bug) | **0.2894** |
| IFE ATT (r=2) | **0.2967** | **0.2968** | — |
| SC ATT (standard) | **0.4144** | **0.4916** | — |
| SC ATT (demeaned) | **0.4743** | **0.4743** | — |
| SDID ATT | **0.3019** | **0.3018** | — |
| HonestDiD (M=2) | [0.361, 0.993] | [0.360, 0.995] | — |

**Notes:**

- Python tabs are shown only where official packages exist (`pyfixest`, `py-did-multiplegt-dyn`).
- IFE, SC, SDID, and HonestDiD do not have official Python packages (`fect`, `sdid_event`/`synthdid`, `honestdid`).
- The standard SC ATT differs between Stata (0.4144) and R (0.4916) due to different package implementations (`sdid_event` vs `synthdid`); the demeaned SC and SDID match exactly.
